Take this free CAT Number System online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Number System chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Number System tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Number System

Factors, divisibility rules, remainders (including large powers), unit-digit cyclicity and number properties.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Factors of N = pᵃqᵇrᶜ number (a+1)(b+1)(c+1).
  • Product of all factors = N^(d(N)/2).
  • Divisibility by 3/9 uses the digit sum; by 11 the alternating sum.
  • Use cyclicity / Fermat–Euler for remainders of big powers.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Missing 1 or the number itself when counting factors.
  • Applying the digit-sum rule to divisibility by 4 or 8.
  • Cyclicity errors on unit digits.

How to get the most from this Number System quiz

Attempt all ten questions in one sitting. Only then check the answers. Switching between solving and checking hides your real accuracy. Read the worked explanation even for correct answers. A right answer reached the slow way still costs time in the exam hall. For every mistake, note the exact step where your method went wrong. Redo that question from scratch two days later. Ten honest questions teach more than fifty solved passively.

faq.q: How many factors does a number have?
faq.a: Write it as pᵃqᵇ…; the count is (a+1)(b+1)…. For 72 = 2³·3², that is 4·3 = 12 factors.

faq.q: How to find remainders of large powers?
faq.a: Use cyclicity of remainders, or Fermat/Euler when the base and modulus are co-prime.
